Definition: from G1458; an accusation, i.e. offence alleged:--crime laid against, laid to charge.
BiblicalUsage: The formal accusation, the crime laid against a man. Lysias found Paul accused of questions of their law but with nothing laid to his charge worthy of death in Acts 23:29, and Festus explains that Rome does not deliver a man to die before he can answer the crime laid against him in Acts 25:16.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's empty charge-sheet is the pattern for every believer — accused, but with nothing worthy of death, because Christ already died.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
